articles.title: ‘Wants electrical engineering over CSE ‘: KCET 2026 topper Srajan BS spills his success secrets
articles.rephrased_article: Srajan B S, a 18-year-old student from Karnataka, secured the second rank in the KCET engineering entrance exam. He achieved this despite not studying for long hours and choosing to focus on consistent study habits rather than marathon sessions. Srajan's preparation involved self-study, weekly tests at his school, and a strong interest in electrical engineering which he pursued after being introduced to it by his mother during the pandemic.  He plans to pursue an undergraduate degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering from IITs or NITs and is considering further studies like Research and MTech.

articles.title: At Jantar Mantar, Abhijeet Dipke says ‘can’t erase us’ — then ultimatum to Dharmendra Pradhan to resign | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the online youth movement Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), arrived at Jantar Mantar after a delay caused by police interference.  Dipke delivered an ultimatum to Dharmendra Pradhan, Education Minister, demanding his resignation by 5 pm or face continued protests across India. The crowd chanted slogans calling for Pradhan's resignation and the unity of youth. Dipke was lifted onto protestors' shoulders in a celebratory gesture, highlighting the movement's growing momentum.

articles.title: Why Apple’s AI strategy may be the biggest focus at its developer conference next week | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Apple is expected to unveil its new AI strategy at WWDC, focusing on how it plans to integrate AI into its devices and services. The company will showcase an upgraded Siri powered by Google's Gemini AI technology, aiming to deliver a more personalized experience across Apple products.  While Apple has historically focused on privacy-first approaches, the company is facing pressure to leverage AI for everyday user needs and create seamless interactions with AI agents. Whether Apple can successfully integrate AI into its ecosystem and overcome consumer skepticism remains to be seen.

articles.title: Why pangolins are vital—and why Nagaland villages are working to protect them | Pets-animals News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Indigenous communities in Nagaland are increasingly turning to traditional laws and grassroots action to protect pangolins, a trafficked mammal. The United Sangtam Likhum Pumji (USLP), the apex tribal body of the Sangtam Naga community, imposed a ban on pangolin hunting across 42 villages in Kiphire district. Conservationist Indrajit Ghorpade emphasizes that protecting pangolins is crucial for ecological balance and warns that their disappearance can trigger cascading effects on forests, agriculture, and biodiversity. He stresses the importance of local participation and cultural change to effectively combat illegal wildlife trafficking, habitat loss, and hunting driven by traditional beliefs and demand for pangolin scales and meat.

articles.title: CJP at Jantar Mantar: How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's protest hub
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday to protest irregularities in examinations and demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The protest, organized by online youth movement Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founder Abhijeet Dipke,  was a symbolic move as it took place at the site where social activist Anna Hazare began his hunger strike against corruption in 2011. The CJP's first on-ground action follows its rapid rise to prominence online after being inspired by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's courtroom comment comparing some youth to cockroaches.  The protest is part of a long history of demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, which has hosted protests against corruption, farm distress, and other social issues.

articles.title: The Moons of Uranus May Hold the Key to Finding Missing Planets | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Icarus researchers analyzed 122 scenarios of planetary instability to assess how the moons of Uranus might have evolved. The study concluded that the current characteristics of Uranus' moons are best explained by episodes of violent instability, likely occurring at least twice: once due to an impact and again during encounters with giant planets. This instability is most likely linked to the existence of one or more missing planets that were ejected from the solar system.  The research suggests that these missing bodies could have influenced the current structure of the solar system, leaving behind clues in the form of unusual moons like Miranda, which may be remnants of a larger body.

articles.title: Importance of being Satish Poonia: Why BJP’s key Rajasthan Jat face is its Rajya Sabha pick | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP has nominated Satish Poonia, a prominent Jat leader, to the Rajya Sabha from Rajasthan as a way to appease the community while keeping him away from direct involvement in state politics. This move comes after the BJP's 2024 Lok Sabha election loss in Rajasthan where the INDIA alliance swept the Jat belt and the party faced criticism for its handling of Jat concerns, including the denial of tickets to prominent Jat leaders and a perceived lack of representation. Poonia has been instrumental in navigating internal power struggles within the party, particularly against former Chief Minister Vasundhara Raje, but his influence may be limited by the BJP's desire to avoid alienating traditional vote banks.

articles.title: Another Setback For AIADMK, Former Ministers, MLAs Join Vijay's TVK, tamil nadu politics
articles.rephrased_article: Four former AIADMK ministers and ex-MLAs joined the ruling TVK party in Chennai on Saturday, following a series of setbacks for the AIADMK after the April 23 election. The defectors, including Udumalai K Radhakrishnan, MC Sampath, Kadambur C Raju, and NR Sivapathi, joined in front of TVK General Secretary Anand and General Secretary for election campaign management Aadhav Arjuna. This latest move follows a trend of AIADMK members joining TVK, including former ministers Vellamandi Natarajan and Anandan, as well as former MLAs.

articles.title: 'No community should live in fear': British MP backs Southampton Sikhs amid rising hostility after Vickrum Digwa's conviction | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Independent MP Adnan Hussain expressed solidarity with Southampton's Sikh community after reports of increased fear and intimidation following the murder of 18-year-old student Henry Nowak. Hussain stated that no group should be blamed for the actions of an individual, urging the government to prioritize the safety of the Sikh community and provide necessary reassurance.  Gurdwara Khalsa Darbar, a representative body for the Southampton Sikh community, reported increased racial abuse and hostility towards residents following Digwa's conviction, leading to cancelled events and fears among members.

articles.title: Crypto-Funded Chinese Peptide Labs Are Booming | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta has been quietly storing dormant face recognition code on its smart glasses, a feature known as NameTag. xAI, a company developing AI technology, is asking a federal judge to force four people suing the company over deepfakes to drop their pseudonyms and litigate under their real names. Meanwhile, Google has rolled out a new Android feature aimed at combating AI-powered impersonation scams.  The Manhattan Institute, a right-wing think tank, is pushing legislation that would turn minor protest offenses into felonies. Researchers have discovered a new browser side-channel attack called FROST that fingerprints other tabs and apps on your device. Anthropic, an AI firm, is helping the NSA with offensive hacking using its powerful Mythos tool.  Bill Pulte has been tapped as acting director of national intelligence while Donald Trump considers other candidates for the permanent position.

articles.title: Norway Crown Princess Put On Waitlist For Lung Transplant
articles.rephrased_article: Crown Princess Mette-Marit of Norway has been placed on a lung transplant waiting list due to her worsening pulmonary fibrosis.  The condition, diagnosed in 2018, has led to significant decline in her lung function and increased scar tissue in her lungs. A compatible donor and priority status are required for the surgery, but there is no guarantee she will receive it. Her husband, Crown Prince Haakon, recently cut short a trip to Japan to be with his wife, while their daughter, Princess Ingrid Alexandra, has also joined her mother in Norway to support her.

articles.title: Ukraine Drone Strikes: Watch: Ukrainian drones hit St Petersburg region again; Russia claims capture of Kharkiv village - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine launched long-range drone strikes deep inside Russia, targeting a military facility near St Petersburg and an oil depot in the Krasnodar region.  Zelenskyy stated that these attacks were aimed at "the enemy navy’s arsenals and a base in Kronstadt," while authorities in St Petersburg advised residents to stay indoors due to potential disruptions. The strikes follow a previous attack on an oil terminal near St Petersburg, as both sides continue long-range drone campaigns with fresh attacks reported on both sides of the conflict.

articles.title: 2 Best Bluetooth Trackers of 2026, Plus Honorable Mentions | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Chipolo, a company known for its Bluetooth trackers, has secured exclusive collaborations with Apple and Google.  The company offers a range of products including the Chipolo Pop, Loop, and Card, as well as bundles compatible with both iOS and Android devices. These trackers use Bluetooth connectivity and GPS to help users locate their belongings. While some trackers like the Apple AirTag offer robust location tracking capabilities, they also raise privacy concerns due to potential misuse.  Tile, another popular tracker brand, has a wide variety of forms including stickers, key rings, and wallets. The article highlights the importance of choosing a tracker that fits your needs and lifestyle while considering factors such as battery life, range, and compatibility.

articles.title: Adani Enterprises Ltd Plants 1.6 Million Trees To Turn Chhattisgarh Coal Mine Green
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Enterprises Ltd. has planted over 1.6 million trees at its Parsa East and Kanta Basan (PEKB) mine in Chhattisgarh, aiming to restore mined land and boost biodiversity. The company's greening project involves replicating native species like Sal, Mahua, and Tendu, with a survival rate of about 88% for the re-planted trees. The Union Coal Ministry praised the initiative as a "remarkable" example of responsible mining practices.  This restoration effort is part of a broader program that includes community development initiatives focused on education, healthcare, and livelihoods in the region.

articles.title: Made In Pakistan Bedsheet Sold At Pune Religious Fair? Viral Video Sparks Probe
articles.rephrased_article: A woman in Pune, India, has accused vendors at a religious fair of selling Pakistani-made goods, including a bedsheet she purchased. The Centre banned imports from Pakistan following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. The police are investigating after the viral video sparked outrage and prompted the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation to take action against vendors.

articles.title: Ozempic, Fitness Apps And Olive Oil: Inside India's $170 Billion Wellness Rush
articles.rephrased_article: India's wellness market is rapidly expanding, projected to reach $170 billion by 2026. Driven by a generation prioritizing prevention over treatment, consumers are embracing technology like fitness apps and wearable devices, as well as healthier food choices and lifestyle modifications.  The growing popularity of GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide, while promising for weight management, is also raising concerns about potential risks if used without proper medical supervision. Experts emphasize the need for a holistic approach to health that combines technology with traditional practices. This shift in consumer behavior has led to a focus on nutrition and cooking oils, with olive oil becoming increasingly popular as consumers prioritize healthy food preparation.  While some experts express reservations about the industry's focus on symptom management rather than root causes, there is widespread agreement that health is no longer just a goal but an integral part of personal identity in urban India.

articles.title: Madhya Pradesh Man Attacks Teen's Face With Axe 20 Times, Tries To Hang Her, Arrested
articles.rephrased_article: In Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district, Dharmendra Parihar, an obsessed and jilted lover, brutally attacked a 17-year-old girl with an axe, injuring her severely. He then attempted to hang her from the roof of her house before she fell to the ground. The incident prompted villagers and the victim's family to block a major road demanding strict action against Parihar and his family.

articles.title: France's 'patriotic' banquets rile hard left
articles.rephrased_article: Le Canon Français, a company that organizes large feasts in France, has become the center of controversy. The events, which feature local cuisine and wine, have been accused by La France Insoumise (LFI) of being racist and exclusionary due to alleged chanting and insults towards immigrant staff. LFI also points to the involvement of an ultra-conservative entrepreneur, Pierre-Edouard Stérin, as evidence of a hidden agenda.  However, organizers of the banquets deny these accusations, stating that they are simply reviving a traditional French custom and that their rules prohibit offensive behavior. The controversy has sparked calls for local authorities to stop the events, with some cities initiating investigations into alleged racial provocation.

articles.title: ‘Badge of honour’: Israeli settlers shrug off global condemnation | Occupied West Bank News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite EU sanctions against Israeli settler groups and their leaders, including Bezalel Smotrich, the movement has dismissed the penalties as "ridiculous" and "banal."  Daniella Weiss of the group Nachala also rejected the sanctions. The actions of these entities, which include high-profile figures like Weiss, Regavim, and the Amana cooperative association, have been met with indifference from the targeted individuals and organizations. Activists argue that the EU measures are ineffective in curbing settler violence against Palestinians, highlighting the deep state complicity and the impunity enjoyed by these groups.  The lack of international pressure has emboldened the alliance between the Israeli government and the settler movement, fostering a sense of entitlement and superiority among settlers who see themselves as divinely ordained to control the West Bank.

articles.title: Isro: Indian space scientist Nandini Harinath's Mars mission sari at US's Smithsonian museum
articles.rephrased_article: Nandini Harinath, an Indian space scientist, wore a vibrant red and blue silk sari on December 1st, 2013, the day India's Mangalyaan spacecraft was launched into orbit. The sari is now displayed at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C., alongside other artifacts from significant space missions.  The museum curator, Matt Shindell, chose the sari to represent India's success in its Mars mission and Harinath's role as a female pioneer in the field of space exploration.

articles.title: ‘Well-deserving’: Agarkar on why Shreyas Iyer is India’s new T20I captain
articles.rephrased_article: India's BCCI announced Shreyas Iyer as the new captain of its T20I team, replacing Suryakumar Yadav. The selection committee cited Iyer's consistent performances and leadership experience over the past few years as reasons for his elevation.  The decision comes after a period in which Iyer has not played a T20I since 2023 despite strong franchise cricket performances. Ajit Agarkar, chairman of selectors, emphasized that the appointment was based on merit and Iyer's consistent batting record. The move signifies a shift in direction for India's shortest-format side ahead of the next global cycle.

articles.title: Ukraine Drone Strikes: Watch: Ukrainian drones hit St Petersburg region again; Russia claims capture of Kharkiv village - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine launched long-range drone strikes deep inside Russia, targeting a military facility near St Petersburg and an oil depot in the Krasnodar region.  Zelenskyy called for an end to the war, stating that Russia must stop its attacks on life.  Russia's Defence Ministry claimed it intercepted 376 Ukrainian drones nationwide while also reporting the capture of the village of Shevchenko in Ukraine's Kharkiv region. The strikes come amidst continued drone campaigns and fighting along largely static front lines.

articles.title: Jordan World Cup 2026 preview: Players to watch, group matches and squad | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jordan is making its World Cup debut after reaching the finals of the 2023 Asian Cup and 2025 Arab Cup. The team, led by coach Jamal Sellami, will face formidable opponents like defending champions Argentina in Group J.  Star player Mousa Tamari is a key attacking threat for Jordan, who are considered underdogs but have shown strong form in qualifying with 32 goals scored. Their group also includes Austria and Algeria. The team's hopes of reaching the knockout stages may be challenging given their low FIFA ranking and tough competition.

articles.title: J&K Health Minister takes exception to Mehbooba touring AIIMS, says ‘suffering from political amnesia’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sakeena Itoo, Jammu and Kashmir Health Minister, criticized former Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti for visiting the under-construction AIIMS, Awantipora site.  Itoo accused those who delayed the project of now attempting to claim credit for its progress. Mufti Muhammad Sayeed, a PDP leader, had envisioned the project in 2015. Ms. Mufti visited the site and requested J.P. Nadda, Union Health Minister, to expedite its completion.

articles.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Singh Mann reviews preparations for rollout of Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhagwant Singh Mann, the Chief Minister of Punjab, announced the launch of the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna, a financial assistance program for eligible women in the state. The scheme will provide every eligible woman with ₹1,000 per month and women from Scheduled Caste categories with ₹1,500 per month.  Mann emphasized that the initiative aims to strengthen women's financial independence and ensure their dignity and self-respect.  The program is expected to benefit around 97% of women in Punjab, with a budget allocation of ₹9,300 crore.

articles.title: Envoys call for ‘rules-based global order’ in era of ‘paradox and polarisation’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: EU, Australia, and India envoys at The Hindu Huddle 2026 emphasized the importance of a rules-based international order and economic integration. They highlighted the growing India-EU and India-Australia partnerships as key drivers for future cooperation, with EU Ambassador to India Harve Delphin advocating for collaboration with countries demonstrating intent, capability, and willingness to cooperate.  Australian High Commissioner to India Philip Green stressed the need to strengthen existing rules while acknowledging that global rulemaking has slowed but not stopped. Former Indian Foreign Secretary Nirupama Rao urged India to maintain its influence through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasizing its pivotal role in the Indo-Pacific region.

articles.title: Indian mission in U.K. condemns disruption at Chief Justice Surya Kant event - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The High Commission of India in London condemned an individual's disruptive behavior at a lecture by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on artificial intelligence and international law. The event, held at Birkbeck, University of London, saw a heated exchange over a question about dissent within India, which was cut short by the moderator.  The statement emphasized that respectful engagement is crucial in public discourse, even when differing opinions arise. Justice Kant, during his address, highlighted the importance of legal frameworks and ethical considerations in ensuring technology's responsible deployment.

articles.title: 13 out of 14 Ministers in Karnataka Cabinet are crorepatis; face criminal cases - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, and 13 other Ministers in the reconstituted state cabinet have declared assets exceeding ₹206.15 crore, according to an analysis by Association for Democratic Reforms and Karnataka Election Watch. All 13 ministers have criminal cases against them, with some having serious charges.  The highest asset holder is Shivakumar, while U.T. Khader Fareed has the lowest declared assets.

articles.title: Modest growth in State’s Own Tax Revenue emerges as weak spot in T.N.’s economy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu experienced a modest economic growth rate of 10.83% in 2025-26, but its State Own Tax Revenue (SOTR) growth was only 6.8%.  The increase in SOTR to ₹1.92 lakh crore from ₹1.80 lakh crore was attributed to the GST rate rationalization implemented in September 2022 and below-par compliance among traders. The Finance Minister, Thangam Thennarasu, had anticipated a revenue shortfall of around ₹9,600 crore for 2025-26 due to this issue.  However, an economist believes that consumption will eventually boost tax collections once the economic growth is driven by exports or broad-based activities.

articles.title: Anthony Head: British actor Anthony Head dies at 72, leaving a legacy across Buffy, Ted Lasso and Merlin | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Head, a British actor known for his roles in "Buffy the Vampire Slayer" and "Ted Lasso", passed away at 72 from complications related to pneumonia.  He was surrounded by loved ones during his death, which was announced by his daughters, actors Emily and Daisy Head. Head had a long career spanning decades across television, theatre, and film, appearing in iconic British advertising campaigns, popular dramas, and beloved fantasy series. He is remembered for his distinctive voice, commanding screen presence, and ability to portray both charming and complex characters.  His legacy will continue through the many productions he helped bring to life.

articles.title: Watch: Cockroach Janta Party Founder Abhijeet Dipke lands in India ahead of Jantar Mantar protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has arrived in India ahead of planned protests. The party plans demonstrations to address key public issues and mobilize supporters.

articles.title: $24 billion 'trust test' for Trump? Khamenei aide seeks frozen assets, warns war could take 'another dimension' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsen Rezaei, military adviser to Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, stated that a potential peace deal between the United States and Iran hinges on the Trump administration releasing $24 billion in frozen Iranian assets.  He argued that this release would be a test of trust for both countries, while warning against renewed conflict and suggesting Iran would expand its response if attacked again. Rezaei also emphasized Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and proposed joint management with Oman, along with financial contributions from all parties involved. Despite expressing skepticism about the durability of any future agreement with the United States, he believes Iran is prepared for a potential military confrontation.

articles.title: Two men convicted of stabbing Iranian TV presenter in London ‘on order of Tehran’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Two Romanian nationals, Nandito Badea and George Stana, were convicted of wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm for stabbing Iranian TV presenter Pouria Zeraati outside his home in Wimbledon. The attack was described as a "deliberate, targeted act of violence" involving months of planning and surveillance, with prosecutors alleging the assault was part of a wider campaign against dissident Iranian media personnel abroad.  The court heard that the attackers were effectively "proxies" used in a broader strategy of harassment targeting journalists critical of Tehran. The case has raised concerns about escalating intimidation campaigns targeting dissidents in Britain.

articles.title: Consumer rights panel in Kerala orders boutique to pay ₹58,350 for delayed gown delivery as photoshoot called off - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kollam, Kerala
articles.rephrased_article: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kollam, Kerala, ordered a boutique to pay ₹58,350 to a customer after it failed to deliver a customized gown for a pre-wedding photoshoot on time. Jennifer Shah, the customer, filed a complaint against Eha Designs Private Limited and its Managing Director, alleging a deficiency in service that led to the cancellation of her scheduled photoshoot. The court ordered the boutique to refund the full price of the gown and pay compensation for emotional distress.

articles.title: “You and your fake husband....": Candace Owens accuses Laura Loomer of lying about her marriage in explosive social media feud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens have escalated their public feud, exchanging personal attacks after Loomer questioned Owens's motives for traveling to Russia.  Loomer accused Owens of seeking political asylum and suggested she was "auditioning" to be a female Edward Snowden. Owens responded with accusations about Loomer's marriage claims, mocking her recent vacation photos and calling out her alleged use of a fake husband. The exchange has drawn significant attention on social media, intensifying the rivalry between two prominent conservative figures.

articles.title: Gurgaon deploys IIT-backed AI sewer sensors in posh colonies to stop monsoon waterlogging | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) is installing advanced monitoring sensors across critical sewer lines to prevent waterlogging and sewer overflows during the upcoming monsoon. The project, in collaboration with AIResQ, a startup incubated at IIT Gandhinagar, uses sensor-based systems to monitor real-time technical parameters.  The MCG aims to provide citizens with better sewerage services by identifying potential overflow situations and allowing field response teams to address blockages before they escalate. This initiative prioritizes vulnerable locations across the city, including upscale colonies like Sushant Lok and Golf Course Extension Road, as well as critical traffic corridors.

articles.title: Oil India’s latest gas find could unlock more hydrocarbon reserves in Andaman offshore | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: OIL India Ltd. announced its second natural gas discovery in the Andaman offshore region, located around 15 kilometers off the eastern coast of the Andaman Islands. The discovery was made at the Vijayapuram-3 exploratory well and follows a previous gas strike at the Vijayapuram-2 well. Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri expressed optimism about the basin's potential as a key hydrocarbon-producing zone, highlighting India’s growing success in offshore exploration efforts. Industry experts believe these discoveries could encourage further exploration and appraisal work to assess the region’s hydrocarbon potential.

articles.title: Cockroach Janta Party protest LIVE: 'Youth of the country will no longer fear' Abhijeet Dipke leads students, youth at Jantar Mantar protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police and paramilitary forces have been deployed across key locations in the national capital as members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) began a protest at Jantar Mantar. The protest is being led by Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the satirical online "Cockroach Janta Party", who arrived from the United States to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over examination-related lapses.  Education reformer and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has pledged to join the protest if the minister does not step down by June 5th.

articles.title: US Bill Seeks To End H-1B Visa Route To Green Card
articles.rephrased_article: Congressman Chip Roy introduced the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act, which aims to overhaul the H-1B visa program. The bill proposes ending the pathway to permanent residency for H-1B holders and scrapping the optional practical training (OPT) program. It also seeks to shorten the duration of H-1B visas from six years to two, prioritize higher-salary applications, and require applicants to demonstrate a residence abroad.  The legislation is backed by US Tech Workers, the Immigration Accountability Project, and the Federation for American Immigration Reform.

articles.title: National Awards for e-Governance 2026 | UPSC Knowledge Nugget
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government has announced the winners of the 29th National Conference on e-Governance, recognizing excellence in e-governance initiatives. The awards include a trophy, certificate, and an incentive for Gold awardees.  This year's winners are projects from various ministries including the Agriculture Ministry's AgriStack platform, the Consumer Affairs Ministry's e-Jagriti portal, and the Prayagraj Mela Authority's conduct of the Mahakumbh 2025. E-governance in India has evolved since computerization in the 1970s, with key milestones including the establishment of the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and the launch of the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP).  Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), a set of foundational digital systems, plays a crucial role in modern society. India's DPI is built on the JAM trinity—Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment, and widespread mobile phone penetration.

articles.title: US Iran War: Missiles, Sirens: Videos Show Kuwait, Bahrain's Response To Iranian Attacks
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the United States engaged in a tit-for-tat escalation of attacks across the Gulf region.  Iranian military spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari blamed the US for escalating tensions, advising Kuwait to alter flight paths and urging citizens to avoid airports. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) intercepted six of seven missiles launched by Iran, with no US personnel harmed. While Iran claimed damage to a US 5th Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, CENTCOM refuted these claims.  The attacks follow an attack on Kuwait's international airport and come amidst ongoing tensions over the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian oil exports.

articles.title: Turkish gang member convicted over plot to murder man outside family's London restaurant after £100,000 demand | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Beytullah Gunduz, 39, was found guilty of conspiracy to murder Onur Guzel, 38, who was shot outside his family's restaurant in Dalston, east London. The shooting occurred after Gunduz accused the victim's family of paying a rival gang £100,000 and demanded an equivalent payment. Prosecutors stated that the attack was linked to a long-running feud between the Hackney Turks (also known as the Bombacilar) and the Tottenham Turks.  The court heard that Gunduz orchestrated the shooting after the victim's family refused his demand. The case involved multiple incidents of violence against the victim's family and restaurant, including shootings and threats. Detective Inspector Iain Wallace from the Metropolitan Police condemned the attack as "calculated and ruthless" and said Gunduz showed a "complete disregard for the safety of both the victim and the wider community."

articles.title: Cockroach Janta Party stages protest, demands Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation: 7 things you need to know | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) are protesting at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, demanding the resignation of Union Minister of Education Dharmendra Pradhan. The group claims Pradhan is responsible for recent national-level exam paper leaks, including NEET.  The protest was granted permission by the Delhi Police after founder Abhijeet Dipke arrived from the United States and the party has received support from several public figures, including social activist Sonam Wangchuk and actor Prakash Raj.

articles.title: KCET Results 2026: Websites to check
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Exam Authority (KEA) will activate the KCET results link at 2 pm today, allowing candidates to check their scores on cetonline.karnataka.gov.in and karresults.nic.in.  A total of 3.1 to 3.2 lakh candidates appeared for the exam, with Tanisha Karthik topping the engineering exam. The results are provisional and candidates must download their marksheets from DigiLocker to enable mark retrieval for merit determination. After the results are released, students will participate in online counselling to choose their preferred colleges.

articles.title: Rare Caracal Spotted In Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park After Decades
articles.rephrased_article: A Caracal, one of India's rarest wild cats, has been recorded in camera trap footage inside Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park after decades. The sighting is being hailed as a positive indicator for the park's ecological health and biodiversity.  Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav described the event as a major achievement for wildlife conservation efforts in the state, attributing it to Project Cheetah's role in restoring the ecosystem. Wildlife experts view this development as significant because the presence of a top predator like the Caracal often indicates healthy prey populations and a functioning ecosystem.

articles.title: HP introduces ZGX Fury GB300, an AI workstation for large-scale models | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: HP unveiled the ZGX Fury GB300 workstation, powered by Nvidia's Grace Blackwell Ultra platform. Designed to bring data center-class AI capabilities to enterprise desktops, the system can support models with up to one trillion parameters and features a large unified memory pool of up to 784GB.  This allows for local processing of AI models and datasets without relying heavily on external storage or cloud infrastructure. The workstation is expected to appeal primarily to large enterprises who require local AI processing for security, compliance, or performance reasons.

articles.title: More than 1,000 Indians deported from U.S. in 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced that 1,076 Indian nationals have been deported from the U.S. this year, marking a significant increase compared to 2025 when 3,567 individuals were deported.  Mr. Randhir Jaiswal, MEA spokesperson, stated that both sides are committed to combating illegal migration and are actively engaged in discussions regarding deportation, migration, and mobility. These discussions aim to address the issue of illegal migration while ensuring legal migration is not negatively impacted.

The CJP claims it has attracted millions of supporters across social media platforms and is calling for Pradhan's removal from the Union Cabinet.

articles.title: Moving fast to close ‘open-ends’; first tranche of India-US trade deal by mid-July: Piyush Goyal | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Piyush Goyal, India's Commerce Minister, announced that the country and the US will sign the initial phase of their trade agreement by mid-July.  Donald Trump, US President, stated that a deal is in progress and he has confidence in the relationship between the two countries. The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) led a delegation to India from June 1st to 4th to discuss the trade agreement. Experts warn that Section 301 tariffs are more powerful than previous measures, giving the USTR wide powers to impose restrictions and retaliate against unfair trade practices.

articles.title: Stonehenge mystery may be closer to being solved as scientists trace Altar Stone’s epic journey | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sheffield Hallam University and Curtin University researchers suggest that glaciers during the last Ice Age may have transported part of the Altar Stone from Scotland to Doggerland, a prehistoric landmass beneath the North Sea.  The study, published in the Journal of Quaternary Science, proposes that Neolithic communities then transported the stone the remaining distance to Stonehenge. While no direct evidence exists for glacial transport to southern England, researchers suggest a combination of coastal routes, rivers, and overland transport may have been involved.

articles.title: Farah Khan stunned by Terence Lewis' surreal Salvador Dalí bathroom, throne-like commode
articles.rephrased_article: Terence Lewis, a celebrity choreographer and reality show judge, recently gave Farah Khan, a filmmaker-choreographer, a tour of his opulent Mumbai house. The home features luxurious yet elegant decor elements like metallic accents on the entrance door, plush seating in white and beige tones, and a black piano.  Ishitta Arun, an artisan from Jaipur, sourced an antique-style door with detailed carvings for the living space. Farah Khan joked that the bathroom resembled a set from a Sanjay Leela Bhansali film, inspired by the surreal, molten-style basin designed by Terence Lewis in homage to Salvador Dalí.  The tour also included a cozy study and a kitchen with a striking chandelier made of tea kettles.

articles.title: TMC parliamentary split ‘just a matter of time’: As Mamata fights back, cracks grow | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee is facing growing dissent within the Trinamool Congress (TMC), with 60 of its 80 MLAs in West Bengal signaling rebellion.  Senior TMC leader Sukhendu Sekhar Roy believes a similar reaction could occur in the Lok Sabha, where the party has 28 MPs and faces potential defections under anti-defection laws. The rebel faction is seeking to retain Mamata Banerjee as chairperson of the party, while others within the party are calling for her removal from leadership positions.  The situation remains fluid with some rebels expressing a desire to remain under Mamata Banerjee's leadership but disagreeing with Abhishek Banerjee's role as national general secretary.

articles.title: Penguin pulls plug on Joe Sacco’s book on Muzaffarnagar riots | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Penguin Random House India has pulled the distribution of Joe Sacco's graphic novel, "The Once and Future Riot," which chronicles the 2013 Muzaffarnagar communal clashes. While the book is available online through UK-based wholesalers, some South Delhi bookstores have imported copies directly from the UK. articles.title: CM Adityanath launches Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam mega plantation campaign - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, launched a "Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam" mega plantation campaign on World Environment Day. The campaign, dedicated to mothers, aims to address environmental concerns by encouraging citizens to plant trees in their honor and contribute to forest conservation efforts.  Adityanath emphasized the need for collective action to protect the environment and highlighted simple measures like avoiding single-use plastic to prevent damage. He also urged citizens not to harm existing trees and to plant at least one tree on every important occasion, referencing the significant number of saplings planted in Uttar Pradesh over the past nine years.

articles.title: Supreme Court denies bail to Haryana travel blogger accused of spying for Pakistan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court dismissed the bail application of Haryana-based travel blogger Jyoti Malhotra, accused of sharing sensitive information with Pakistan. The court found no grounds for release due to the seriousness of the allegations and the nature of her activities, including alleged contact with Pakistani intelligence operatives.  Ms. Malhotra, who ran a YouTube channel called "Travel-with-Jo", is facing charges under the Official Secrets Act and Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The Haryana Police allege she was attempting to act as an asset for Pakistani intelligence, exchanging video footage of strategic installations with them.

articles.title: Ramalinga Reddy resigns from Ministry, says he is ‘humiliated’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ramalinga Reddy, a senior Congress legislator from Bengaluru, resigned after being denied the Bengaluru Development portfolio by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.  He stated that he would not personally submit his resignation but would do so through an official channel.  Reddy, who has been influential in East and North Bengaluru, expressed disappointment over the decision and claimed a promise made by Shivakumar to give him the portfolio was broken. Supporters of Reddy staged protests in his constituency.  Former Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil urged leaders to address the issue justly.

articles.title: Kharge files nomination papers for Rajya Sabha polls from Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mallikarjun Kharge, president of the All India Congress Committee, filed his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha election from Karnataka, accompanied by Rahul Gandhi. The other two candidates are Mansoor Ali Khan and Pawan Khera.  The elections will be held on June 18th with the Congress party expected to secure three seats. Discussions regarding portfolio allocation among ministers were reportedly underway during a car ride.

articles.title: After initial denial, CBSE invited ethical hacker to plug gaps in IT system - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) invited ethical hacker Nisarga Adhikary, 19, to help address security vulnerabilities in its IT ecosystem.  A team of cybersecurity experts from the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) worked for two weeks at the CBSE headquarters, patching critical vulnerabilities found in the OSM portal and the re-evaluation portal. The IIT teams identified seven to eight critical vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass and unauthorized administrative access, in the portals developed by COEMPT Eduteck.  The team also discovered that the external vendor had severely misconfigured cloud storage buckets, keeping unsecured backups of student answer scripts on their servers.  To address these issues, the IIT experts set up a "Red Team versus Blue Team" dynamic to test and defend the portals. The CBSE has issued an advisory to departments to consider cybersecurity hygiene when hiring tech vendors.

articles.title: Two killed, four injured in roof collapse at underground coal mine in Madhya Pradesh’s Shahdol - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) workers were killed and others injured when a portion of the roof collapsed in an underground coal mine in Madhya Pradesh's Shahdol district. The accident occurred at Bangwar mine, where workers were constructing a stopping wall, trapping them under debris. Dhanpuri Police Station House Officer (SHO) Khem Singh Pendro confirmed two workers died and four others were injured. Rescue teams and officials are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Great Nicobar project meant to benefit Adani, it’s not about defence: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the BJP’s claim that the Great Nicobar Island project is strategic, alleging it's a ploy to benefit industrialist Gautam Adani.  Gandhi launched an online petition urging citizens to join his campaign titled “we choose green over greed,” highlighting concerns about ecological destruction and displacement of local communities. He argued that expanding the naval air station INS Baaz would be a more appropriate strategic move, while accusing the government of prioritizing commercial interests over environmental protection. Mallikarjun Kharge, Congress president, echoed these sentiments, criticizing the government's environmental record and deforestation rates.  Gandhi called for sustainable development in Great Nicobar, contrasting it with the proposed project that he believes would harm the island’s environment and indigenous communities.

articles.title: Kochi Corpn. to issue notice to CSML over streetlight maintenance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kochi Corporation is preparing a notice to Cochin Smart Mission Limited (CSML) regarding the alleged malfunctioning and poor upkeep of LED streetlights installed by it. The Mayor V.K. Minimol expressed concerns about the erratic functioning, alleging inferior control panels and relaxed tender conditions. CSML sources countered that less than 200 lights were non-functional, attributing the issues to electrical line faults requiring KSEB intervention.  The Corporation plans to extend maintenance coverage to 6,000 old streetlights outside the CSML project.

articles.title: Pre-monsoon works spared city of major waterlogging: Kochi Mayor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mayor V.K. Minimol stated that pre-monsoon works implemented by the Corporation successfully prevented flooding in areas previously prone to waterlogging, including Madhava Pharmacy Junction and M.G. Road.  The city experienced minimal flooding due to heavy rainfall and high tide, with minor waterlogging issues addressed through drain cleaning and removal of slabs covering drains. The Mayor dismissed protests from the Democratic Youth Federation of India as "political drama" while assuring public input is considered in ongoing pre-monsoon work efforts.

articles.title: Best Running Shoes, Tested and Reviewed (2026): Saucony, Adidas, Hoka | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: WIRED editors have compiled a list of the best running shoes available. The article highlights several models, including the Adidas Pro Evo 3 and Saucony Endorphin Speed 5, as well as options from brands like New Balance, Brooks, and Hoka.  The editors recommend considering factors such as comfort, stability, and durability when choosing running shoes. WIRED also provides tips for shoe care and replacement guidelines.

articles.title: 12 hospitalised after ammonia leak in ice plant at Munambam in Kochi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Twelve people were hospitalized after an ammonia leak at a private ice plant in Munambam, Kerala. The incident occurred when a slab fell on the ammonia receiver tank, damaging a valve and releasing the gas. Fire and rescue services personnel contained the leak within two hours. Residents near the plant experienced breathing difficulties and burning sensations, prompting authorities to advise them to stay elsewhere for the day.

articles.title: US Court Strikes Down Trump Policies Targeting Immigrants From 39 Countries
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge ruled that the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and its US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) violated immigration laws by implementing unlawful policies that barred people from 39 countries from receiving decisions on asylum, work permits, green cards, and citizenship.  The ruling was issued by Chief US District Judge John McConnell in Providence, Rhode Island, who found the USCIS's hold on processing applications to be arbitrary and based on "anti-immigrant sentiments." The judge emphasized that these individuals had adhered to legal processes and were not at fault for the delays. This victory for immigrant service organizations and labor unions was hailed as a reaffirmation of the principle that the federal government cannot discriminate against people based on their origin.

articles.title: BJD criticised Centre for alleged delay in approval of Odisha Coastal Highway Project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Biju Janata Dal criticized the Narendra Modi Government for allegedly delaying and altering the Odisha Coastal Highway Project. The party expressed disappointment over the approval of only two stretches of the project, from Rameshwar to Konark and Konark to Paradip, with an allocation of ₹8301 crore, while excluding vast coastal regions like Bhadrak and Balasore. Sanjay Kumar Das Burma, a BJD leader, stated that this decision was discriminatory and hindered the project's progress due to repeated changes in alignment, cancellations of tenders, and administrative neglect.

articles.title: 'Seniors will win in Pro League': Sardar after IND defeat PAK in U18 Asia Cup
articles.rephrased_article: India defeated Pakistan 5-3 in the semifinals of the men's U-18 Asia Cup hockey on Friday, advancing to the final.  The match saw a dramatic back-and-forth with both teams trading goals throughout the game. Sardar Singh, current coach of the U-18 men’s team, expressed confidence that this winning streak will continue in upcoming pro league games against Pakistan.  India will face Japan in the final on Saturday.

articles.title: Four months after Ajit Pawar’s death, rival NCP factions to hold separate foundation day events | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions, led by Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Ajit Pawar, will hold separate foundation day events in Mumbai on June 10th.  Sunil Tatkare, NCP state president and MP, announced the celebrations for the faction led by Sharad Pawar. The Sharad Pawar-led faction will celebrate its foundation day with a meeting of INDIA bloc constituents on June 8th under the theme "Loyalty to ideology, dedication to people". Both factions have continued to observe June 10th as their foundation day following Ajit Pawar's death in January.

articles.title: Ranveer Singh’s father thanked us for support, says Poonam Dhillon as film body lifts ban | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) has revoked its non-cooperation directive against Ranveer Singh after the actor's father expressed gratitude to Poonam Dhillon, President of the Cine & TV Artistes’ Association (CINTAA), for her support.  Dhillon had previously opposed the FWICE directive and stated that it was unwarranted due to Singh's reputation and commitment to his work. She also revealed that she spoke with Ranveer Singh's father, who expressed appreciation for their support and confirmed a positive resolution between Excel Entertainment, led by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani, and the actor.

articles.title: US Iran War Live High-Risk Iran Mission For Uranium Donald Trump Considered, Then Walked Away From
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump considered but rejected a proposal to send American troops into Iran to retrieve enriched uranium, deeming the mission too risky and requiring extensive military equipment.  He stated that the operation would have taken at least two weeks and involved transporting large amounts of equipment into the country. Trump suggested that the United States still possesses the capability to carry out such an operation if needed, but emphasized that it is not necessary due to the material being "entombed" and posing no immediate threat.

articles.title: The 300-Reaction Mineral: Why Persistent Fatigue and Cyclical Migraines Are Warning Signs From Your Body
articles.rephrased_article: Nutritionist Deepsikha Jain highlighted three possible signs of low magnesium levels: palpitations, anxiety, and panic attacks. articles.title: JD Vance Blames EU Migration Policy For UK Student's Murder
articles.rephrased_article: US President JD Vance blamed British Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government for the death of a white student, Henry Nowak, by a Sikh man and called for "righteous anger" in response.  Vance, who has been critical of European migration policies, suggested that Nowak's murder was a result of "civilizational decline" caused by an "invasion" of migrants. The British government rejected US intervention in the case, stating that they did not want the killing to be used to create further division.

articles.title: ‘Pervasive fear’ grips Gaza as Israeli attacks persist despite ceasefire | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's military has continued its attacks on Gaza, despite a ceasefire in place since October, resulting in the death of a young woman and injuries to at least 15 others.  The attacks have fueled fear and panic among Palestinians, who are questioning the effectiveness of the ceasefire.  Palestinian factions are meeting in Egypt to discuss the future of Gaza, including the disarmament of Hamas and the transition to the second phase of the ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: Smart Border Project Is In Final Stage, Says Amit Shah
articles.rephrased_article: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the rollout of Smart Border pilot projects across India's international frontiers to address evolving security challenges, including drone-based smuggling and human trafficking. The program will integrate district administrations, police authorities, and local institutions into a coordinated security mechanism.  Shah emphasized that lasting border security requires participation from all stakeholders and highlighted the government's commitment to strengthening infrastructure and modernizing fencing systems. He also stressed the importance of environmental protection as a mass movement and praised BSF personnel for their dedication in challenging conditions.

articles.title: Allahabad High Court Grants Bail To Rape, Murder Accused Over Lack Of Evidence
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court granted bail to Manoj, an accused in a rape and murder case, due to the lack of scientific evidence linking him to the crime. The court directed the UP chief secretary to address these issues and improve FSL capabilities.

articles.title: Iran footballers issued US visas for World Cup, says White House | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s World Cup football players have been granted US visas, just 10 days before their opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles. While some members of the Iranian team’s technical and administrative staff have not yet received their visas, the US has not officially stated its opposition to the team staying on its territory. articles.title: Moderate quake hits Himachal districts; tremors felt in neighbouring States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 5.0 magnitude earthquake struck near the Kangra-Chamba border in Himachal Pradesh on Friday night, causing tremors felt in parts of Punjab, Haryana, and Chandigarh. The epicenter was located near Dhar Godoi in Kangra, with a depth of 5 km.  The meteorological office reported that the tremor occurred at 10:04 pm and caused residents to evacuate their homes in panic. No injuries or significant damage have been reported so far.

articles.title: Trump makes pitch to farmers hard-hit by tariffs, high prices in Wisconsin | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump visited Wisconsin to address concerns of farmers impacted by tariffs and the economic fallout from the US-Israel war with Iran.  He sought to bolster support for Republican US Representative Derrick Van Orden, who has aligned himself with Trump's agenda. Trump assured farmers that the administration was "largely finished" with the war and promised lower fertilizer and gas prices. The visit comes amidst low approval ratings for Trump, as several Republicans have expressed concerns about his recent actions potentially alienating voters concerned about the economy.

articles.title: Himanta Sarma expands Assam Cabinet, balances new faces and loyalists, groups and regions | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Sarma, Assam's Chief Minister, expanded his cabinet to 17 members on Friday. The new ministers include several former Congress leaders who joined the BJP with Sarma, such as Ajanta Neog and Pijush Hazarika, along with Sushanta Borgohain, Biswajit Daimary, Ranoj Pegu, and Rameshwar Teli.  The cabinet also includes representatives from Southern Assam's Barak Valley and the Koch Rajbongshi community. The expansion reflects a balance between new faces and loyalists, while maintaining representation from various regions and communities within Assam.

articles.title: Gadchiroli farmers intensify agitation against airport, industrial projects | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers in Gadchiroli are protesting against the government's land acquisition for an airport, industrial projects, and mining activities. The farmers allege that fertile farmland is being acquired without their consent or proper gram sabha approval.  Vivek Khobragade, leader of the Azad Samaj Party, stated that over 6,000 farmers have joined the protest, demanding the cancellation of land acquisition for these projects and immediate measures to address the issue of wild elephants. Ashish Jaiswal, co-guardian minister of Gadchiroli, visited the protest site and assured farmers their concerns would be addressed.  Avishyant Panda, the Gadchiroli Collector, stated that the land acquisition process provides stakeholders an opportunity to express their reservations but denied claims of misinformation and provocation.

articles.rephrased_article: A special court in Jalgaon, India, sentenced a man to death for the rape and murder of a 13-year-old tribal girl and her two minor siblings. The judge deemed the crime "rarest of the rare" due to its brutality and premeditated nature. Ujjwal Nikam, former Special Public Prosecutor who is now a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, argued for the death penalty. articles.title: JiDion rejects Alex Rosen partnership after his $10,000 ChudTheBuilder bond contribution raises questions - The Times of India

articles.title: Nick Polom reaches divorce agreement with Malena Tudi following $400,000 legal battle but one settlement detail grabs attention - The Times of India

articles.title: The US Has a Plan to Combat Screwworm. It Involves a Lot More Flies | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) confirmed the presence of New World screwworm in a calf in southern Texas, marking its return to the US after 60 years.  To prevent an outbreak, the USDA is deploying sterile screwworm flies through targeted releases and air drops. The technique, known as the sterile insect technique, was previously successful in eradicating the pest from Curaçao and aims to disrupt the female fly's mating cycle. The USDA is investing in facilities to increase production of sterile flies, but experts warn that the spread of the screwworm could continue.

articles.title: Iran Claims Fired Missiles On 2 US Warships, CENTCOM Says "Did Not"
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's military claimed to have fired warning missiles at two US destroyers in the Gulf of Oman, forcing them to leave the area. The Iranian military attributed this action to "maritime misconduct and harassment" as well as US naval forces' alleged involvement in hijacking commercial vessels. However, US Central Command denied these claims, stating that no attack occurred and that its forces are operating freely in regional waters while enforcing the US counterblockade on Iranian ports.

articles.title: After Delhi Hotel Fire Kills 21, Big Move Against Government Officials
articles.rephrased_article: Following the Malviya Nagar fire tragedy that killed 21 people, the Delhi government has warned officials may face financial liability for negligence.  The government will invoke provisions of the Revenue Recovery Act and Disaster Management Act to recover losses from property owners and negligent officials. The move comes as investigators examine whether regulatory failures, illegal construction, and safety violations played a role in the tragedy. District Magistrates will be empowered to coordinate enforcement and identify responsibility across departments. The government has also ordered inspections of hotels, guest houses, restaurants, and Bed and Breakfast establishments across Delhi.

articles.title: Why Washington is reducing visa processing across Africa | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States plans to centralize visa processing across Africa, reducing the number of embassies and consulates handling applications from about 50 locations to roughly 20. Routine visa interviews would be moved out of many posts and concentrated in regional hubs, with cities like Nairobi, Johannesburg, Addis Ababa, Accra, and Dakar expected to play larger roles. While the proposal does not change who can get a US visa, it could increase travel costs and logistical hurdles for applicants, potentially discouraging some from applying. The changes are part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to prioritize efficiency, oversight, and security considerations in US foreign policy.  This move is being viewed with mixed reactions across Africa, with some seeing it as another barrier to mobility while others view it as part of a larger trend of tightening restrictions on African citizens seeking entry into the United States.

articles.title: Major Abhilasha Barak Honoured With UN's Military Gender Advocate Award
articles.rephrased_article: Major Abhilasha Barak, India's first woman combat helicopter pilot, received the UN 2005 Military Gender Advocate of the Year Award for her efforts to promote women in peacekeeping. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres praised Barak as a role model and highlighted her work in building trust with local communities, developing early-warning networks, and empowering women through vocational training.  The UN also presented awards to two Indian peacekeepers who died while serving in the Democratic Republic of Congo and South Sudan.

articles.title: "No Point": Putin Turns Down Zelensky's Rare Appeal To Meet Him
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin ruled out meeting Volodymyr Zelensky anytime soon, stating he would continue Russia's military offensive until its war goals are met.  Zelensky proposed a direct meeting to end the four-year war, gaining support from key Western leaders including US President Donald Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron.  The Russian leader also rejected claims that the Russian economy was falling apart, stating that Russia is pursuing a "sovereign" economy.

articles.title: Russia To Launch Own Smaller Version Of Elon Musk's Starlink In 2027
articles.rephrased_article: Russia plans to launch its own satellite broadband system, Iks Holding, in 2027. The development comes after successful Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian targets, which some experts attribute to Starlink's resilience against jamming.  SpaceX's Starlink network has been banned in Russia.

articles.title: Russia’s Putin says ‘no point’ meeting Ukraine’s Zelenskyy for now | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin of Russia rejected an offer for in-person talks with Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian president, stating he sees no point in such a meeting at this time.  Putin insisted that military action would only cease when Russia achieves its goals and suggested that experts should work on developing solutions before any future negotiations. Zelenskyy responded by saying Putin's rejection showed the Kremlin had no desire to end the war and that it was a weak response. The ongoing conflict in Ukraine, now in its fifth year, has largely stalled due to Russia's insistence on retaining seized territory.

articles.title: Trump admin’s cancellation of wind energy projects causes business turmoil | Renewable Energy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration canceled several offshore wind energy projects, causing turmoil for developers and states. TotalEnergies, a French energy giant, agreed to withdraw from four leases in exchange for payments totaling over $2 billion. Seven northeastern states are suing the government, arguing that the cancellation was arbitrary and detrimental to their energy needs. The Interior Department cited security concerns as justification, but the lawsuit claims these concerns were already addressed before awarding the leases. TotalEnergies maintains it withdrew due to cost considerations and believes the technology is not yet suitable for the US market. This action has raised concerns about investment predictability in renewable energy under a new administration and could impact future offshore wind projects.

articles.title: Partnerships That Deliver: India And Denmark's Collaboration On Environment In Action
articles.rephrased_article: The India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership offers a novel approach to water governance, moving beyond traditional project-based partnerships and focusing on systems thinking. UNOPS and the Danish Environmental Protection Agency play key roles in bridging global knowledge with local implementation, supporting India's Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) by strengthening institutions and fostering community engagement. The partnership has proven successful in improving water service reliability and sustainability across multiple states, demonstrating that long-term system stability requires a holistic approach that addresses policy, institutions, and community needs. This approach is particularly relevant for large-scale infrastructure projects like JJM, which aims to ensure access to safe drinking water for all by 2028.

articles.title: Is the latest US ceasefire deal for Lebanon meaningless? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a US-brokered ceasefire, Israel and Hezbollah continue fighting in Lebanon.  The truce announcement did not include Hezbollah, which has continued its attacks, while Israel continues to launch airstrikes. Experts are uncertain about the future of the conflict and its impact on Lebanese civilians.

articles.title: Judge strikes down Trump bar on asylum, visa processing for 39 countries | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge has struck down sweeping restrictions imposed by the Trump administration on immigration processing for 39 countries, ruling that they put immigrants' lives in "indeterminate legal limbo". Judge John McConnell condemned the policy as motivated by "anti-immigrant sentiment" and argued that the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) used "pretextual concerns of 'national security'" to mask discriminatory practices. The judge criticized the administration's claims about national security, stating that the restrictions were based on the "happenstance of their birth".  The ruling is a victory for immigrant rights groups who have been critical of the Trump administration's policies towards legal immigration.

articles.title: Anthropic urges AI labs to pause, warns humans risk losing control | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, a leading AI company, has urged AI labs to pause development of advanced AI systems due to concerns about rapid technological advancement outpacing societal control mechanisms. The company believes a coordinated global mechanism is necessary to verify if other companies have truly halted or slowed their work and prevent malicious actors from exploiting the slowdown for competitive advantage.  This proposal comes amidst growing fears that self-improving AI could pose significant risks, as evidenced by recent research showing how AI tools can be used to create "worms" capable of adapting hacking strategies to spread across networks and compromise systems.

articles.title: Weather Updates LIVE, 5th June 2026, IMD Weather Forecast, Rainfall in Delhi, Kerala, Karnataka, Kerala Monsoon, Southwest Monsoon: Heavy To Very Heavy Rainfall Likely Over Kerala, Karnataka
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms are expected across India, with the Southwest monsoon setting in over Kerala on Thursday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red alerts for five districts in Kerala and orange alerts for several other states.  The IMD predicts isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall (7-20cm) over Kerala and Karnataka and isolated heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu during the coming week, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely to continue over northeast India. Authorities are urging residents to take precautions as strong winds and flooding are possible in affected areas.

articles.title: Supreme Court orders status quo on deportation of two women declared foreigners by Assam tribunal | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has stayed the deportation of two women, Saleha Khatun and Sarbhanu Begum, who were declared foreigners by the Foreigners Tribunal in Assam. The court issued a stay order on Friday, directing that their status quo be maintained until July 16, 2026, when the case will be further heard. The women claim they are impoverished and illiterate, working as maids, and have been detained since March 2, 2026, after being declared foreigners by the tribunal. They argue that their claims of lineage to pre-1971 India were rejected on trivial grounds.

articles.title: Nick Polom reaches divorce agreement with Malena Tudi following $400,000 legal battle but one settlement detail grabs attention - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nmplol and Malena Tudi, a well-known streaming couple, have finalized their divorce after a costly legal battle. The agreement resulted in an equal split of most assets except for Starforge Systems, Nmplol’s computer company, which received a separate allocation.  The court also denied Tudi’s request for $5,000 per month in spousal support for five years. This high-profile divorce has sparked discussions about asset division, financial implications of divorce, and the impact of public scrutiny on relationships.

articles.title: Putin says there is no point meeting Zelensky over ending Ukraine war
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin stated there is "no point" in meeting Volodymyr Zelensky to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, calling Zelensky's request for direct negotiations "rude."  Putin reiterated that a ceasefire would only allow Ukraine to regroup and that Russia demands agreements on territorial concessions from Kyiv before any peace talks can occur. Zelensky responded by stating that Russia is choosing war again and that many are disappointed with Putin's refusal to meet.  The Ukrainian president also noted the recent attacks on Russian territory, including one on St Petersburg, as a sign of his country's resolve.

articles.title: France opens ‘war crimes’ probe into Israel’s treatment of Gaza activists | Human Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: France has opened a preliminary investigation into suspected “torture” and “war crimes” related to the alleged mistreatment of French activists who participated in a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. The probe was initiated following a referral from the foreign ministry, after activists accused Israel of severe mistreatment during their detention.  The incident has drawn condemnation from several countries, including France, which banned Itamar Ben-Gvir, the Israeli National Security Minister, and summoned the Israeli ambassador over his mocking video of the flotilla activists.

articles.title: Relief for JEE qualifiers hit by CBSE OSM Row: IIT Roorkee allows seat allocation even below 75%

The decision comes in response to concerns raised about errors in CBSE’s On-Screen Marking system for Class 12 evaluations, which have left some students ineligible for IIT admission despite clearing JEE Advanced. Students must submit their revised scorecards to orgjee@iitr.ac.in once they are available.

articles.title: This Summer Travel Season Could Forever Alter the Future of Sustainable Aviation Fuel | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Miller, a Vancouver-based aviation analyst, and his family canceled their summer trip to Rome due to the global fuel shortage caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The situation has led to rising jet fuel prices and flight cancellations across various airlines. United Airlines, Delta, American Airlines, and Cathay Pacific are among those using sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), which can cut emissions by up to 80 percent, but currently costs more than conventional jet fuel.  The industry is hopeful that SAF will help bridge the gap between rising prices and increased demand for summer travel. World Energy, a US conglomerate, previously produced SAF but has scaled back production due to resource constraints. However, recent events have highlighted the need for alternative fuels like SAF.

articles.title: How a Citizen Science Organization Aims to Preserve the Places It Brings Tourists to Study | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: In the Peruvian Amazon, Richard Bodmer leads research at a protected area that is managed by Indigenous communities.  His work with Earthwatch Expeditions, which connects tourists with scientists conducting long-term research projects, has helped to demonstrate that people can coexist with nature and contribute to conservation efforts. The research has led to the establishment of community reserves, where sustainable resource use has been proven to conserve biodiversity while supporting local economies. Tourists participate in data collection activities like bird surveys and learn about Indigenous cultures and conservation practices. This approach is seen as more sustainable than traditional "fortress conservation" which often displaces Indigenous communities.

articles.title: How to Spot Greenwashing Claims When You Travel | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have identified five key categories of greenwashing in tourism: eco-certifications, inadequate waste management, misleading carbon offsetting claims, destination-based overconsumption, and the use of the “green development” label.  To cut through the noise, independent and robust certification systems are crucial, along with looking for credible third-party certifications from programs like the GSTC and EarthCheck. When evaluating a hotel's green credentials, look for evidence of specific waste reduction efforts, details about energy sources and water conservation practices, sourcing of local materials, and engagement with local communities.  Be wary of vague claims and unsubstantiated information, and consider the role of ownership in a company's sustainability practices.

articles.title: ‘Gurdwara is empty’: Sikhs scared to come out of houses in Southampton after Vickrum Digwa killed Henry Nowak - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sikhs in Southampton are experiencing heightened fear and intimidation following the murder of student Henry Nowak by Vickrum Singh Digwa, a Sikh man who was sentenced to life imprisonment. Community leaders have reported increased racial abuse, with incidents occurring at workplaces, public spaces, and even within gurdwaras. This fear is fueled by the ongoing public discussion surrounding the murder case, which has been heavily criticized by community members who feel targeted and unfairly blamed for Digwa's actions.

articles.title: US Senate passes $70bn ICE funding bill: What comes next? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera

articles.title: Somalia declares order restored after two days of fighting in Mogadishu | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Somalia’s federal government declared that order has been restored in Mogadishu after two days of fighting between government forces and opposition fighters. Despite the government’s claims of restored order, the opposition vows to continue their fight.

articles.title: Norway's crown princess on lung transplant waiting list, palace says
articles.rephrased_article: Norway's Crown Princess Mette-Marit has been placed on a lung transplant waiting list due to her incurable lung disease. articles.title: Inside Army's 'Hifazat' Exercise To Combat J&K's Natural Disaster Risks
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Army conducted a disaster response exercise called 'Hifazat' in Rajouri district, testing coordination among various agencies including the Army, Police, NDRF, SDRF, civil administration, and local community. articles.title: An ice cream parlour survives Gaza’s genocide and gives seven students hope | Gaza News | Al Jazeera

articles.title: Three men jailed over theft of 'priceless' golden helmet from Dutch museum

The Dutch authorities recovered the helmet and two of the bracelets after striking a plea bargain with two suspects, while the third bracelet remains missing. articles.title: Lawsuit challenges US ‘third-country’ deportations to Equatorial Guinea | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera

articles.title: Hooch deaths: ‘Perfect case of government negligence; what was learned from 2015 Malwani liquor tragedy?’ asks Congress | Pune News - The Indian Express
